cab11b660e: A slash chord is two chords played together
25008d2716: MythA slash chord is still one chord; it just names the lowest note.
07b7330f5f: The bass must be the chord's root
df2de8a848: MythThe root is the most stable, but thirds, fifths and passing notes can all go in the bass.
3d373a1d49: C/G and C have the same notes
baf4b8798c: FactBoth are C, E and G; only the lowest note differs, and the feel changes with it.
e16f662927: Only bass players need to understand bass lines
a79fee920f: MythWhen you play and sing, you're the whole band, and a bass line makes one guitar sound fuller.
2a0253e148: FactA bass stepping down brings out nostalgia and wistfulness most easily.
b35fb1f339: The more passing notes, the better
185cc9c159: MythThe accompaniment's job is to set off the voice; few and well placed is best.
9f4bf756cb: Split into two parts: half the class plays only the bass, half strums the treble strings, then swap. It's also the "Canon-style" bass movement common in classical music.
